comments.author: IMAYousaf
comments.why: Concise, informative look at culture behind outdoor kindergartens
comments.text: Hi everyone. This is a very concise (11:32) video that goes over some of the culture and thinking around outdoor kindergartens. I believe that it is quite informative: [VIDEO] I believe that the best part about these schools is that early on they explicitly teach teamwork and understanding limits. It's quite shocking culturally seeing kids whittling with sharp knives and climbing rather precarious trees but it seems to work well.

comments.author: Symbiote
comments.story: German Kindergarten Campouts Test Helicopter Parents (2015)
comments.why: Small documentary on Danish outdoor kindergartens
comments.text: They're also very popular in Denmark, and the rest of Scandinavia. Description in English: [LINK] And a small documentary: [VIDEO] An equally significant difference for me, coming from the UK, is that there are men working in childcare. My window overlooks a street where a lot of nursery and primary school groups walk past on their way to the park, and my guess is half the adults are men. I was 9 years old in England when I first had a male teacher.

comments.author: eesmith
comments.why: Example of a forest approach in Denmark
comments.text: See also [LINK] on a similar yard in Wales. See [LINK] . This is more derived from the Lady Marjory Allen pedagogy (mentioned in the The Atlantic article as a distinct heritage from the kibbutz approach). She got the idea from the Dutch skrammellegepladsen - [LINK] . I recall watching a video from the mid-20th century about one of them, but can't find it. For a recent US/NYC example, [LINK] . For a more outdoors/forest approach in Denmark - [VIDEO] . > "Who lets kids play with oleanders?" I do? I have no idea what an oleander is (beyond "plant"), so don't know why they are a problem. :)
